subject: Floor realignment and earnback mechanics — pricing exhibit amendment
messages:
From: Samira Khan <s.khan@helixcare.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Owens <tim.owens@helixcare.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed adjustments to Exhibit B (floors / earnback)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the last call. Our procurement & finance teams reviewed the pricing exhibit and have two concrete asks we want to put on the table for consideration before legal proceeds with formal redlines: 

1) Temporary floor relief for Q3: HelixCare is projecting a slower-than-expected rollout in July/Aug and would like the committed minimum fee floor for the first full quarter of service (Q3) reduced from the baseline in Exhibit B by 40%. We see this as a temporary measure tied to onboarding cadence.

2) Earnback structure in lieu of pure credit refunds: instead of a straight refund if usage misses the minimums, we want an earnback mechanism where HelixCare can earn back the waived floor over the following 4 quarters based on percent-of-commit realized (e.g., 25% earnback at 50% of committed usage, scaling to 100% at 100%+). We believe this preserves revenue predictability while sharing onboarding risk.

Attached is our annotated Exhibit B (Helix_ExhibitB_redline.pdf). Tim is on copy for legal language. Can you confirm whether Redwood would consider a time-limited floor reduction with the earnback ladder described? If not, please propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Sr. Procurement Manager | HelixCare

Subject: Re: Proposed adjustments to Exhibit B (floors / earnback)

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear proposal and the annotated exhibit. Looping in Karthik (pricing/legal) and Rishi (finance) so we can respond with a proposal we can take to our contracts team. High-level reaction: we appreciate the earnback framing — it’s preferable to a straight refund. We have two immediate concerns to validate internally:

- The size of the temporary discount (40% for a full quarter) — we need to model the revenue impact against our minimum commitment schedules and compute the earnback schedule that preserves unit economics.
- The true-up cadence and the operational mapping to usage bands (monthly vs. quarterly) — we generally prefer quarterly true-ups for predictability, but we can be flexible.

Karthik / Rishi — can you review Helix’s proposed ladder and suggest Redwood counter language that preserves a revenue floor (cap on cumulative credits) and a clear schedule for suturing the waived amounts via earnback? Also flag any clawback/cap language we should include so we don’t create an open-ended liability. I’ve attached a working version of the pricing schedule that includes placeholders for the earnback matrix (pricing-schedule_proposal_v2.docx).

Samira — we’ll aim to get a concrete counter by EOD tomorrow. Is Helix flexible on the true-up being quarterly vs. monthly? We find quarterly reduces settlement churn.

Best,

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed adjustments to Exhibit B (floors / earnback)

Marissa / team — reviewed Helix’s annotated exhibit and propose the following counterpoints we can offer in an amendment (draft language below):

1) Temporary Floor Relief: Redwood will agree to a one-quarter temporary floor reduction not to exceed 40% of the baseline minimum fees, limited to the customer’s first full quarter of service following go-live. After that quarter, the baseline floor reverts to the committed minimum unless the earnback schedule is triggered.

2) Earnback Ladder (sample mechanics):
- If average quarterly usage >= 25% of committed band: 25% of waived floor is earned back (credit converted to reduced fees)
- If >= 50%: 50% earnback
- If >= 75%: 75% earnback
- If >= 100%: 100% earnback
Earnback to be evaluated on a rolling quarterly basis for up to 4 quarters. Earnback credits are applied to future invoices and capped at the total waived amount; any unearned residual will not be refundable.

3) Cumulative Cap & Liability Limit: Total cumulative credits or waived fees applied under this clause shall not exceed the greater of (a) 120% of the waived floor amount or (b) USD 250,000. This creates a hard cap on Redwood’s liability.

4) True-up cadence: Redwood prefers quarterly true-ups. If Helix requires monthly reconciliation for operational reasons, we can accommodate but will pro-rate earnback thresholds to preserve equivalent behavior.

I’ve drafted suggested contract language and included example math in the attached doc (pricing-schedule_proposal_v2.docx). Please review and advise before I share a redline to Helix.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Dir, Pricing & Legal Ops | Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — that construct is very close to what we had in mind. Two quick clarifying Qs from our finance team: 

1) The cap math: can you confirm whether the \"greater of (a) 120% of the waived floor amount or (b) USD 250,000\" is cumulative across the 4-quarter earnback period or applied per-quarter? We assume cumulative but want written confirmation.

2) Invoice application: will earnback credits apply to the next invoice cycle after measurement (i.e., quarter N usage measured -> credits applied to invoices in quarter N+1)? Helix prefers a predictable next-quarter credit application.

If those are as expected, Tim will circulate a short redline to accept the form and we can proceed to DocuSign.

Best,
Samira

Samira — thanks, confirmed on both items:

- The cap is cumulative across the 4-quarter measurement window (hard cap on total credits).
- Credits will be applied to the invoice cycle immediately following the measurement quarter (quarter N measured -> credits on quarter N+1 invoices).

We’ll prepare a short amendment that (a) implements the one-quarter temporary floor relief up to 40%, (b) adds the 4-quarter earnback ladder above, and (c) includes the cumulative cap language and quarterly true-up cadence.
